findings.title: The new then_wrapped comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry…
findings.claim: The new then_wrapped comment says _outgoing_queue_ready is exceptional if an entry failed, but a failed entry resolves its done promise with a value. Exceptions come only from withdraw(ex) or _negotiated abort in stop_send_loop.

findings.title: The new doc says the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed,…
findings.claim: The new doc says the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, and commit 3 says closing one half leaves it never shut down. The code shuts the connection down on other paths too.

findings.title: The test does not assert that the hook is refused with closed_error
findings.claim: The test does not assert that the hook is refused with closed_error. It accepts a successful hook call too and checks only whether a put() reached the socket.

findings.title: In the test, cleanup comes after assertions and blocking calls that can bail out early
findings.claim: In the test, cleanup comes after assertions and blocking calls that can bail out early. If the BOOST_REQUIRE on hooks.size() fails, or the hook throws something other than closed_error, then release_close is never set, sink_closed is never awaited, and server_done is dropped. The unclosed sink is then destroyed and hits SEASTAR_ASSERT in ~sink_impl.

findings.title: The test waits on close_entered_cv with no timeout
findings.claim: The test waits on close_entered_cv with no timeout. If stream_close() never reaches write_buf.close() (for example if the new queue-drain wait hangs), the test blocks until the external ctest timeout instead of failing with a message.

findings.title: The new fix waits for frames that send() accepted before _stream_closing was set (the…
findings.claim: The new fix waits for frames that send() accepted before _stream_closing was set (the queue_drained path). No test covers that path. The test also covers only one variant: client side, with the sink closing last. Server-side stream_close and the close_source()-last path are not covered.

findings.title: The fixture test_data_sink_impl hard-codes buffer_size() to 8192 instead of forwarding…
findings.claim: The fixture test_data_sink_impl hard-codes buffer_size() to 8192 instead of forwarding to _inner.buffer_size(), even though every other method forwards. This changes the output_stream buffering seen by production code.

findings.title: `auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory
findings.claim: `auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory.hooks.back();` keeps a reference into a std::vector that negotiate() keeps appending to.

findings.title: The test factory uses const_cast to mutate itself inside the const negotiate()
findings.claim: The test factory uses const_cast to mutate itself inside the const negotiate(). The local convention for test compressor factories is a `mutable` member.

findings.title: None of the three commits carry the DCO `Signed-off-by:` trailer that the repository's…
findings.claim: None of the three commits carry the DCO `Signed-off-by:` trailer that the repository's contribution guide requires.

findings.title: If the test fails between parking the close and releasing it, the test hangs instead of…
findings.claim: If the test fails between parking the close and releasing it, the test hangs instead of failing. A BOOST_REQUIRE or a non-closed_error exception from the hook skips release_close.set_value(). The close_entered wait also has no timeout.

findings.title: _stream_closing adds a second send-refusal flag next to _error, but only…
findings.claim: _stream_closing adds a second send-refusal flag next to _error, but only connection::send() checks it. client::enqueue_zero_frame(), described as 'the enlightened copy of connection::send()', still checks only _error, and the public error() accessor does not reflect the new flag.

findings.title: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from…
findings.claim: The new stream_close() comment says 'Nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on'. That is a non-local invariant, and nothing enforces it.

findings.title: The continuation parameter `f` in stream_close() shadows the outer local `f` that is…
findings.claim: The continuation parameter `f` in stream_close() shadows the outer local `f` that is being assigned.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl and test_socket_impl are thin pass-throughs that copy the…
findings.claim: test_connected_socket_impl and test_socket_impl are thin pass-throughs that copy the whole connected_socket_impl/socket_impl interface by hand, including 17 forwarding overrides. test_socket_impl duplicates the existing rpc_socket_impl wrapper.

findings.title: test_data_sink_impl::buffer_size() returns a hard-coded 8192 instead of forwarding to…
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl::buffer_size() returns a hard-coded 8192 instead of forwarding to _inner, unlike every other member of this pass-through.

findings.title: The test depends on the client compressor factory having been negotiated exactly twice…
findings.claim: The test depends on the client compressor factory having been negotiated exactly twice and assumes the last hook belongs to the stream connection. It also records server hooks that are never used.

findings.title: The test relies on a fixed 10 yield() calls to 'let the batch flush poller run'
findings.claim: The test relies on a fixed 10 yield() calls to 'let the batch flush poller run'. Nothing ties that count to when the poller runs, so a fixed build could pass because the regressed write simply hasn't happened yet.

findings.title: The new doxygen blocks on sink and source sit on top of the old plain `// send data Out
findings.claim: The new doxygen blocks on sink and source sit on top of the old plain `// send data Out...` / `// receive data In...` comments, which are now redundant.

findings.title: The stream shutdown contract is written out in three places that must stay in sync:…
findings.claim: The stream shutdown contract is written out in three places that must stay in sync: rpc-streaming.md, the sink doxygen and the source doxygen.

findings.title: The test_sink_state lives on the lambda's stack, but the socket wrappers that reference…
findings.claim: The test_sink_state lives on the lambda's stack, but the socket wrappers that reference it are owned by the stream connection, whose lifetime is managed by rpc.

findings.title: The regression test never covers the second half of the fix: waiting for _outgoing_queue…
findings.claim: The regression test never covers the second half of the fix: waiting for _outgoing_queue to drain before write_buf.close(). A fix that only sets _stream_closing, without the drain, still passes.

findings.title: Commit 1 lands the behavior change without the regression test that proves it
findings.claim: Commit 1 lands the behavior change without the regression test that proves it. The test comes separately in commit 2.

findings.title: Only the client-side stream connection is tested
findings.claim: Only the client-side stream connection is tested. The server stream connection gets the same unguarded hook through a different negotiate() call site, and the test never fires it.

findings.title: stream_close() now waits for _outgoing_queue_ready before calling write_buf
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for _outgoing_queue_ready before calling write_buf.close(), and this wait has no timeout or cancellation. If the front entry is stuck in send_entry(), for example because the peer has stopped reading, or the queue is still waiting on _negotiated, sink.close() and stop() are both delayed. A concurrent stop_send_loop() no longer waits for the queue either, because stream_close() replaced _outgoing_queue_ready with a ready future.

findings.title: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but…
findings.claim: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but other code paths set _error while the drain/close is in flight.

findings.title: The comment justifying the std::exchange says nothing else waits for…
findings.claim: The comment justifying the std::exchange says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready and that stop_send_loop() waits for _sink_closed_future. In fact stop_send_loop() still moves and waits on _outgoing_queue_ready, now the ready placeholder.

findings.title: The new block comment on stop_send_loop and _sink_closed_future serialization is placed…
findings.claim: The new block comment on stop_send_loop and _sink_closed_future serialization is placed above the old comment on the same subject, which was left in place. Two adjacent comments now explain the same interaction.

findings.title: test_data_sink_impl overrides only the API-level-9 put(std::span<
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl overrides only the API-level-9 put(std::span<...>) and has no `#if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL` branch. In builds with Seastar_API_LEVEL < 9 it stays abstract (put(net::packet) is pure) and rpc_test.cc fails to compile.

findings.title: The test keeps a reference into the growable vector client_factory
findings.claim: The test keeps a reference into the growable vector client_factory.hooks and picks the stream's hook by position (back(), size()==2). Any added negotiation would invalidate the reference or select the wrong connection's hook.

findings.title: The new HOOK compressor copies the delegate/empty-frame rule from…
findings.claim: The new HOOK compressor copies the delegate/empty-frame rule from test_compressor_empty_frames' compressor, along with its abort()-ing two-argument negotiate.

findings.title: The test helper types have generic names (test_sink_state, test_data_sink_impl,…
findings.claim: The test helper types have generic names (test_sink_state, test_data_sink_impl, test_connected_socket_impl, test_socket_impl) that hide their specific role: parking data_sink::close() until released and recording put() calls after close.

findings.title: The doc and the source doxygen tell applications to 'drain what is still in flight' as…
findings.claim: The doc and the source doxygen tell applications to 'drain what is still in flight' as the only way to release a source. They don't say this read is unbounded: it completes only when the peer closes its sink or the connection errors.

findings.title: The stream shutdown contract is now written out three times, in doc/rpc-streaming
findings.claim: The stream shutdown contract is now written out three times, in doc/rpc-streaming.md and the sink and source doxygen blocks, in near-identical wording. The old one-line `// send data Out...` / `// receive data In...` comments are left between each new doxygen block and its class.

findings.title: The new rpc::sink doc says the connection is shut down once the source on this…
findings.claim: The new rpc::sink doc says the connection is shut down once the source on this connection has also been read to eof. But _source_closed defaults to true and is cleared only when a source_impl is constructed. If no source was ever created on the connection, closing the sink alone runs stream_close().

findings.title: send() now fails with closed_error ("connection is closed") while connection::error()…
findings.claim: send() now fails with closed_error ("connection is closed") while connection::error() still returns false. _stream_closing is private and not reflected in error(), so the 'is this connection usable' predicate and send() now disagree during the stream_close window.

findings.title: The PR verification runs only rpc_test, while the contribution guide asks contributors…
findings.claim: The PR verification runs only rpc_test, while the contribution guide asks contributors to run test.py and confirm that tests pass at least as well as before.

findings.title: The commit and PR text attribute the crash to the stream connection and say the same…
findings.claim: The commit and PR text attribute the crash to the stream connection and say the same unflushed 141-byte frame also sat on the parent client. The fix changes only stream_close(), and neither text explains why the parent client's pending frame is benign or covered.

findings.title: stream_close() now waits for every previously accepted _outgoing_queue entry before it…
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for every previously accepted _outgoing_queue entry before it closes write_buf and calls stop(). The wait has no timeout or cancellation, and the PR docs and the new 'Closing a stream' section do not mention that sink.close() and the source's final read can now block on queued compressor frames.
